facility_desc: ~822,500 sf warehouse/distribution facility, 19451 and 19535 Waverly Rd (ELHC XIV, LLC building, subleased to Amazon.com.ksdc LLC)
program: City of Edgerton economic development grant paid from the Logistics Park public infrastructure fund (Ordinance 1013 and grant agreement)
issuer: City of Edgerton, Kansas (Ordinance 1013, approved March 2016; summary published 2016-03-30)
notes: Grant of $1,800,000 to Amazon.com.ksdc LLC, paid in semiannual installments (Apr 1 and Nov 1) from 2018 to Nov 1 2027, solely from the public infrastructure fund, not a general obligation. Conditions: Amazon lease of at least 10 years; facility operational; Amazon must keep operating and employ more than a nominal number of staff; city may terminate on uncured breach and owe no later payments; no jobs number in the ordinance. Jobs figure (about 1,000) is from KSHB (saved as kshb_amazon_edgerton_1000_jobs.html), not the ordinance. Realized payments not obtained. Site match: facilities.csv has MKC4 at 19645 Waverly Rd (Gardner) and 19400 Montrose St (Edgerton); the ordinance addresses 19451/19535 Waverly Rd, so the match is probable only. Secondary: https://www.kshb.com/money/business-news/amazon-to-bring-1000-jobs-to-edgerton-kansas (says grant matched by KDOT grant, 'no tax money used', and 10-year abatements for park companies).

facility_desc: Same building: 822,500 sf, 19451 and 19535 Waverly Rd, developer ELHC XIV, LLC
program: Industrial Revenue Bonds (ELHC XIV, LLC Project) Series 2015; IRB structure carries property tax abatement via PILOT in Edgerton
issuer: City of Edgerton, Kansas (bond ordinance not obtained; recited in Ordinance 1013)
notes: Ordinance 1013 recites IRBs of up to $38,000,000 principal for the building (leases dated 2014-12-01); the beneficiary is the developer, Amazon is a sub-tenant. $38M is bond principal (financing), not a subsidy value, so amount is blank. City testimony to the Kansas House Taxation Committee (2017-05-10, saved) says Edgerton IRBs allow property tax abatement with negotiated PILOTs and names Amazon among park tenants. Abatement rate, term and Amazon-specific PILOT not found. KSHB says each park company has a 10-year abatement; a Fox4 item seen only in a search summary quotes the city saying it gives no abatement to Amazon directly (not opened, unverified). Treat as an abatement structure, unquantified. UPDATE 2026-10-31: the bond ordinances are now saved. Ordinance 1005 (passed 2015-12-10, scanned PDF read with local DeepSeek-OCR) authorizes IRBs (ELHC XIV, LLC Project) Series 2015 of not more than $38,000,000 for an approx. 822,500 sf warehouse and distribution facility at 19451 and 19535 Waverly Road, leased by the City to ELHC XIV, LLC (the developer); Ordinance 1036 (passed 2016-09-22) authorizes Series 2016 supplemental bonds of not more than $25,000,000 for the remaining cost of the same building. Neither ordinance names Amazon or states an abatement, PILOT rate or term (those are in the lease and performance agreements, not obtained). The same two ordinances also belong to this one row; do not add them as separate awards.

facility_desc: Amazon fulfillment center, 6925 Riverview Ave (about 850,000 sf, developer RELP Turner LLC, Turner Diagonal at I-70)
program: Unified Government of Wyandotte County/KCK industrial revenue bonds with 10-year 100 percent property tax exemption and a PILOT of $5,000 a year (RELP Turner LLC)
issuer: Kansas Board of Tax Appeals (Order No. 2018-3869-IRBX, 2018-07-18) and Unified Government of Wyandotte County/Kansas City, Kansas
notes: Primary: Kansas Board of Tax Appeals order of 2018-07-18 (text reproduced on vLex, not the BOTA PDF itself) grants exemption under K.S.A. 79-201a Second to the 850,000 sf facility at 6925 Riverview Ave (Parcel 105-055-15-0-20-03-001.00-0), financed with IRBs of $138,010,000 issued 2017-12-13 ($15M land, $119M improvements; city Ordinance O-49-17; public hearing 2016-06-09); exemption runs 10 calendar years, 2018-01-01 to 2027-12-31 or while bonds are outstanding; school district levies are not exempted (SB 19 s.52). Secondary (Wyandotte Daily News 2016-06-09, quoting UG officials; KC Star 2016-06-10): the UG Commission on 2016-06-09 approved a resolution of intent for up to $310,500,000 IRBs, a 100 percent 10-year abatement, a PILOT of $5,000 a year for 10 years, a 1,500-job projection, a $1.68M payment if local/WMBE goals are missed and a $1.5M payment if 1,000 jobs are not provided for 15 years; the tenant was named as Amazon on 2016-06-13. Wyandotte Daily News 2017-10-12 (agenda item): an ordinance to issue not more than $150M of IRBs for RELP Turner LLC, the Amazon project, because the project had meanwhile 'received incentives from the Kansas Department of Commerce' (unspecified). The dollar value of the abatement is not stated in any source; the bond principals are financing, not subsidy value, so amount is blank. The beneficiary of the exemption is the developer/lessor (Amazon is the tenant). Not the same as the 9400 Leavenworth Rd (FOE1) HPIP row, which is a different building. UG commission minutes and the PILOT agreement not obtained.

facility_desc: Amazon distribution center (about 915,000 sf, former Golden Books building north of Coffeyville; opened 1999, closed Feb 2015)
program: City of Coffeyville / Montgomery County incentive package: cash incentives tied to jobs and salary targets plus infrastructure
issuer: City of Coffeyville (Interim City Manager James Grimmett quoted by the Wichita Eagle)
notes: Wichita Eagle 2014-12-03 quoting the interim city manager: in 1999 Coffeyville awarded Amazon $1.2M in infrastructure improvements and $3.3M in cash incentives tied to salary and employment targets (sum $4.5M). Amazon stopped requesting payments in April 2012; the program expired August 2014; Amazon told the city it would not claim the remaining $562,213 ('goodwill gesture'), so the amount actually paid is lower than the $4.5M package (not stated). Wichita Eagle 2014-10-02 gives a different split of the same package: about $4.5M, with $350,000 a year for up to 10 years if employment goals were met plus about $1M for road, water and sewer access. Same package, one row. The Eagle also reports that in 2014 state and local officials offered a retention package 'approaching eight figures' (nearly $10M) and Amazon turned it down; not an award. Site Selection (May 2000) says dollar values were not disclosed at the time. Primary city records (1999 agreement) not obtained.

facility_desc: Amazon last-mile delivery station, 1851 W Water Well Rd (20.07-acre site, Airport Industrial Center Subdivision No. 3)
program: Salina Airport Authority roads and utilities for Airport Industrial Center No. 3, financed with $6,000,000 General Obligation Temporary Notes Series 2025-1 (special assessment benefit district repays)
issuer: Salina Airport Authority (board memo 2026-01-19, Resolution 26-01) and City of Salina
notes: SAA board memo (primary): to meet 'Amazon's accelerated schedule' the Authority built the street and utility network itself and issued $6,000,000 of temporary notes; the work 'enabled the sale of a 20-acre site to Amazon'. Actual costs came in lower, about $1,560,000 of note proceeds remain for reallocation, so spent is roughly $4.44M (derived). Repayment is by special assessments on all benefited landowners (Project 80 benefit district), not by Amazon alone and not a payment to Amazon; whether Amazon bought the land at market price is not stated. Secondary (Salina311 2026-06-08): the City sold general obligation bonds (resized to $12.595M) that include road work tied to the Amazon facility, with Airport Industrial Center No. 3 Phase 1 at about $4.72M, special-assessment supported; this overlaps the $6M and is not added. SAA release 2025-02-13: Amazon bought 20 acres, 90,000 sf facility, at least 100 jobs, $17 an hour. No tax abatement found. Amount is the financing issued for the public infrastructure that serves the site, an upper bound on public support, not value to Amazon.
